clause_text: All employees must read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form on their first working day.
Employees must collect their staff ID badge from Human Resources on Day 1 and wear it visibly at all times while on property.
Employees must use the staff entrance and record attendance on the biometric clock at the start and end of every shift.
New employees are encouraged to complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path within their first 30 days.
Employees must take part in the annual fire drill held at their property.
Chilled food must be kept at or below 5 °C.
Employees must not accept gifts of any value from guests or suppliers.
New employees must complete a six-month probation period, with formal reviews at the end of months one, three and five.
Employees must complete a 30-day check-in meeting with their reporting manager and record it in the HR portal.
Standard working time is 48 hours per week across six shifts; overtime is required to be approved in advance by the department head.
Employees working night shifts must take a paid 30-minute break between 02:00 and 04:00 and must not leave the property during it.
Absence due to illness must be reported to the supervisor at least two hours before the start of the shift.
Grievances must be raised first with the direct supervisor and, if unresolved within five working days, escalated in writing to Human Resources.
Employees may apply for an internal transfer after completing 12 months of service.
Employees are entitled to 30 calendar days of annual leave per year, accrued monthly from the date of joining.
A maximum of 5 unused annual leave days may be carried forward to the next year; any excess days lapse on 31 March.
Annual leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least 14 days before the first day of leave.
Annual leave will not be approved during property blackout dates published by the General Manager, except in documented emergencies.
Sick leave of more than two consecutive days must be supported by a medical certificate submitted within 48 hours of return.
All employees must sign the Code of Conduct declaration before their first shift.
Harassment, discrimination or bullying of guests or colleagues is prohibited and must be reported through the Speak Up line or to Human Resources.
Employees may accept unsolicited gifts from guests up to a value of USD 25; any gift above this value must be declared to the Duty Manager within 24 hours.
Employees must wear the full Aurelle uniform and name badge while on duty, following the grooming standard in Annex A.
Maintenance Technicians are exempt from the uniform standard in Section 4.1 and must instead wear the engineering workwear and PPE required by HSP-01.
Employees must not post photographs of guests, guest rooms or back-of-house areas on personal social media.
Conflicts of interest, including family relationships with suppliers, must be declared to Human Resources in writing.
All employees must complete the Information Security Basics e-learning module before being granted access to any Aurelle system.
Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.
Multi-factor authentication must be enabled for email and for the Property Management System (PMS) before first use.
Users must never share login credentials; every action in the PMS must be performed under the user's own account.
Workstations must be locked whenever they are left unattended.
Suspected phishing emails must be reported using the Report Phishing button and must not be forwarded to colleagues.
Guest or employee personal data must not be copied to USB drives or personal cloud storage.
Any suspected security incident must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately.
Employees whose role involves guest personal data must complete Guest Data Privacy training within their first week.
Guest personal data may only be accessed to deliver the guest's stay or for a documented business need.
A guest's passport or national ID may be scanned only into the PMS; paper copies are prohibited.
Scanned copies of guest identity documents must be permanently deleted from the PMS no later than 7 days after check-out.
Guest identity documents must never be received, photographed or stored on personal mobile phones or messaging apps.
Room numbers and guest names must not be disclosed to callers or visitors; calls are to be connected to the room without confirming the guest's presence.
At Malaysian properties, guests must sign the Personal Data Consent Notice at check-in before any marketing preferences are recorded.
Employee personal files must be accessed only by Human Resources and stored in the HR system, never in shared drives.
Any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data must be reported to the Duty Manager and IT within 1 hour of discovery.
Employees who process payments must complete Payment Card Handling training before operating a payment terminal or cash drawer.
Guest payment cards must never be photocopied, photographed or written down; card details are to be entered only into the payment terminal.
Pre-authorisations must be taken through the terminal at check-in and must not exceed the room rate plus 20% for incidentals.
Each cashier is issued a personal cash float, which must not exceed USD 500 or local equivalent, and must sign for it at the start of the shift.
At the end of every shift, the cash float must be counted by the cashier and a second employee and the result recorded on the Shift Close Form.
Cash variances greater than USD 10 must be reported to Finance on the same day.
Refunds must be processed to the original payment method; cash refunds of card payments are prohibited.
Finance must reconcile the daily card settlement reports against the PMS by 12:00 on the following day.
Every new employee must attend a fire and life safety orientation on their first day.
Employees must know the location of the fire assembly point and the two nearest fire exits for their work area.
On hearing the fire alarm, employees must follow the RACE procedure (Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Evacuate) and must not use the lifts.
All employees must participate in a fire drill every six months.
Supervisory and engineering staff must demonstrate correct use of a fire extinguisher using the PASS technique during practical training.
The Duty Manager must carry the evacuation master key and the in-house guest list during every shift and lead the evacuation roll call.
Front Office must print the list of guests requiring evacuation assistance at the start of every shift.
Workplace injuries, however minor, must be reported to the supervisor and recorded in the incident log before the end of the shift in which they occur.
Safety footwear, gloves and eye protection must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools.
Employees who handle cleaning or pool chemicals must complete Chemical Handling training before first use.
Loads heavier than 20 kg must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley.
The pool must be closed to guests at 20:00 and at any time a lifeguard is not on duty.
Employees assigned to pool duty must hold a valid lifeguard certificate before their first pool shift.
Pool water chlorine and pH levels must be tested and logged every 4 hours during opening hours.
F&B employees must complete Food Safety Level 1 training before handling open food.
Chilled food must be stored at or below 4 °C, with temperatures checked and logged twice per shift.
Hot food held for service must be kept at or above 65 °C and discarded after 2 hours.
When a guest declares a food allergy, the server must check the Allergen Matrix for every dish ordered and inform the chef in person.
Allergy-declared orders must be marked with a purple allergy flag on the kitchen ticket and served by the same server who took the order.
Food handlers must report symptoms of vomiting or diarrhoea and must not work with food until 48 hours after symptoms stop.
Associates should complete the Coffee & Tea Service Fundamentals course within 60 days.
Employees assigned to In-Room Dining must complete In-Room Dining Service training before their first room-service shift.
Room-service orders may only be accepted during the operating hours listed for the property in Annex A; orders outside these hours must be referred to the Duty Manager.
Before delivery, the associate must confirm the guest's name against the room number in the PMS and must not announce the room number aloud in public areas.
Trays and trolleys placed in corridors must be collected within 60 minutes of the guest placing them outside the room.
In-Room Dining associates must demonstrate the knock, announce and wait-for-invitation entry procedure during a role-play assessment.
At check-in, the associate must verify the guest's identity against a valid passport or national ID and scan it into the PMS.
Early check-in up to 2 hours before the standard 15:00 check-in time is free of charge, subject to availability; earlier arrivals are charged 50% of the nightly rate.
Standard check-out time is 12:00; late check-out is charged at 50% of the nightly rate until 18:00 and a full night thereafter.
Late check-out fees may only be waived in line with REV-01 Section 3.4.
Associates must settle the guest folio, obtain the guest's agreement to all charges and close the payment on the terminal before issuing the final invoice.
Replacement room keys may only be issued at Front Office after verifying the guest's identity against the PMS record; other departments must not open rooms for guests.
Associates must complete the PMS Front Desk certification before working a shift alone.

condition: Two or more years of previous front office experience
clause_text: Associates with two or more years of previous front office experience may take the PMS certification test directly without attending the classroom module.
At Residences properties, long-stay guests of 30 nights or more must re-verify their identity document every 90 days.
The night audit must start at 02:00 and be completed before 05:00.
Before running the day-end, the auditor must reconcile all cashier Shift Close Forms against the PMS cash report.
Occupied rooms without a posted room charge must be investigated and reported to the Duty Manager before day-end.
Rate overrides above 15% of the published rate without an approval code must be listed on the Rate Exception Report for Revenue review.
The night audit pack, containing the reports listed in Annex 1, must be saved to the Finance shared folder before 06:00.
Finance must review the night audit pack and clear all exceptions within one working day.
Check-out rooms must be cleaned to the 42-point standard and inspected by a supervisor before being released as Vacant Clean in the PMS.
Supervisors must inspect a minimum of 12 rooms per shift using the room inspection app and record all defects.
Rooms displaying Do Not Disturb must not be entered; if the sign remains after 15:00, the supervisor must inform the Duty Manager for a welfare check.
A welfare check must be performed by two employees, one of whom is required to be the Duty Manager or a Security officer.
Engineering defects found during inspection must be logged in the maintenance system within 30 minutes.
Supervisors should rotate room attendants between floors monthly to balance workload.
All found items must be logged in the Lost & Found register within 1 hour of being found.
Valuables, including cash, jewellery, electronics and documents, must be sealed in a tamper-evident bag and handed to Security in line with the Security SOP.
Non-valuable items must be kept for 90 days and valuables for 180 days before disposal or donation.
Items may only be returned after the owner provides a description matching the register and shows photo ID.
Properties may donate unclaimed non-valuable items to an approved charity.
Technicians must complete Work Permit and Lockout/Tagout training before carrying out any electrical or mechanical work.
Electrical work, hot work and work at height require a signed Permit to Work issued by the Chief Engineer or Duty Engineer.
Electrical work in guest rooms may only be carried out when the room is vacant; if the room is occupied, the guest must be moved or the work rescheduled.
Before starting work, the technician must isolate the energy source, apply a personal lock and tag, and test for zero energy.

condition: Holds a valid hot work certificate
clause_text: Hot work such as welding, cutting or grinding may only be performed by technicians holding a valid hot work certificate, with a fire watch present for 30 minutes after completion.
Guest-room maintenance requests must be acknowledged within 15 minutes and resolved, or the guest updated, within 2 hours.
Complaints must be handled using the CARE model: Calm, Acknowledge, Resolve, Echo back.
Every complaint must be logged in the Guest Incident Log within 30 minutes, including the resolution offered.
Guest Relations Executives and Front Office Associates may offer service recovery up to USD 50 per stay; higher amounts require Duty Manager approval.
The Duty Manager may approve service recovery up to USD 300 per stay; above this amount, the Hotel Manager must approve.
Guest Relations Executives must demonstrate complaint handling in a role-play covering a billing dispute and a room-quality complaint.
Complaints involving safety, discrimination or data privacy must be escalated to the Duty Manager immediately, regardless of value.
Any injury to a guest or employee must be reported to the Manager on Duty (MOD) within 15 minutes.
Suspected data breaches must be reported to the Manager on Duty and the IT Service Desk within 1 hour.
The Duty Manager must notify the General Manager within 30 minutes of any Severity 1 incident, meaning death, serious injury, fire, police involvement or a data breach.
The Duty Manager must complete the Incident Report in the incident system before the end of the shift for all Severity 1 and 2 incidents.
Employees must not speak to the media about any incident and must refer all enquiries to the Communications team.
Duty Managers must complete Crisis Communication training within their first two weeks.
Only rates loaded in the PMS by Revenue Management may be offered to guests; manual rate creation is prohibited.
Rate overrides above 15% of the published rate require an approval code from the Duty Manager or a Revenue Analyst.
Late check-out fees may be waived only by the Duty Manager, and the reason for the waiver must be recorded in the PMS.
Revenue Analysts must produce the daily pick-up and pace report by 10:00 each day.
Forecast accuracy must be reviewed weekly, and variances above 5% must be explained at the weekly revenue meeting.
Group quotes above 10 rooms per night must be evaluated with the displacement calculator before being offered.
All group and event bookings must be recorded in the Sales & Catering system within 24 hours of the enquiry.
Contracts must use the approved Aurelle template; any change to cancellation or payment clauses requires Director of Sales approval.
Group bookings must be secured with a non-refundable deposit of 30% of the total contract value within 14 days of signature.
Banquet Event Orders must be issued to all operating departments at least 7 days before the event.
Sales Executives must demonstrate preparing a complete group proposal, including rate, deposit schedule and cancellation terms.
Sales Executives should conduct at least four client site inspections per month once fully onboarded.
Purchases above USD 1,000 require an approved Purchase Order before the order is placed with the supplier.
Supplier invoices must be matched to the Purchase Order and the goods received note before payment.
City ledger credit above USD 5,000 per account must be approved by the Finance Manager before the account is activated.
Expense claims must be submitted with original receipts within 30 days of the expense.
Group deposits of 25% of the contract value must be received before a booking is confirmed as definite.
Finance Associates must complete a supervised month-end accounts payable close before working independently.
Right-to-work documents must be verified and copied to the personnel file before the employee's first working day.
Personnel files must be created in the HR system within 2 working days of joining; paper files are not permitted.
HR Executives must schedule the new hire's Day 1 orientation, badge issue and uniform fitting before the joining date.
Salary and disciplinary information must not be shared with line managers beyond the minimum necessary for approved HR processes.
HR Executives must demonstrate processing a complete onboarding file, including contract, right-to-work check and probation schedule.
Exit interviews must be offered to every leaver and recorded within 5 working days of the last working day.
System access is requested by the line manager through the IT portal and is granted only after the Information Security Basics module has been completed.
PMS access levels are assigned by role; associates must not request or use a higher access level than their role requires.
Passwords must be at least 10 characters long.
Personal devices must not be connected to the staff Wi-Fi without enrolment in the Mobile Device Management app.
Company email and systems must not be used for personal commercial activities.
Employees may request access to the Aurelle Learning app on their personal phone after MDM enrolment.
Front Office Associates must complete a standard check-in in under 5 minutes once certified.
Front Office Associates are responsible for offering room upgrades using only the rates available in the PMS.
Guest Relations Executives must contact every VIP and returning guest within 2 hours of arrival.
Guest Relations Executives must review the Guest Incident Log at the start of every shift.
Housekeeping Supervisors may open guest rooms for guests who have lost their key card after checking the guest's name.
Housekeeping Supervisors must allocate room attendant sections and brief the team before every shift.
F&B Associates must know the daily menu, specials and allergen information before service begins.
F&B Associates should achieve the Aurelle Service Excellence certificate within 60 days.
Maintenance Technicians may carry out minor electrical repairs in occupied guest rooms if the guest agrees.
Maintenance Technicians must complete the planned preventive maintenance tasks assigned in the maintenance system each week.
The Duty Manager is the senior manager on duty outside office hours and has authority over all operational decisions until relieved.
Duty Managers must complete a property walk-through, including back-of-house areas, at least twice per shift and log it.
Sales & Events Executives are responsible for accounts in their assigned market segment and for meeting the quarterly revenue target set by the Director of Sales.
Sales & Events Executives must hand over each confirmed event to the Events Operations team at least 14 days before the event.
Revenue Analysts are responsible for supporting the Director of Revenue in setting daily rates across all distribution channels.
Revenue Analysts must maintain the competitor rate shop and update it daily by 09:00.
Finance Associates process accounts payable and city ledger transactions and must follow FIN-01 for all approvals.
Finance Associates must complete ERP Finance module training before posting any journal entry.
HR Executives are the first point of contact for employee relations queries at property level.
HR Executives must complete HR System administrator training before creating personnel files.
Yes, you can carry forward up to 10 days of unused annual leave.
Front desk staff can waive the late check-out fee for Aurelle Circle loyalty members.
Guests can use the pool after 20:00 at their own risk if they sign the waiver at Front Office.
Uniforms must be returned to the Uniform Room for laundering; washing uniforms at home is not permitted.
If you are unsure whether a guest's pet can stay, check the Pet Policy (PET-01).
Fire and Life Safety orientation must be completed on Day 1.
Guest Data Privacy training must be completed within Week 1.
All employees must acknowledge the Information Security Policy in the HR portal within their first week.
All mandatory e-learning modules in the onboarding plan must be completed with a pass mark of at least 80% within 30 days of joining.
Employees who fail a mandatory assessment twice must be referred to their manager for a coaching review before a third attempt.
Employees with approval authority must sign the Delegation of Authority acknowledgement before exercising any approval limit.
During peak season, front desk staff may accept photos of guest passports via WhatsApp to speed up check-in.
Please remind your teams to take their breaks away from guest areas.
Partner agents shall present a valid Horizon booking voucher when checking in groups.
